agenda_items.description:
Notices and meeting information are attached to the agenda and minutes, including: availability of simultaneous interpretation and accessibility accommodations; in camera meeting procedures; information items not subject to discussion; personal information disclaimer for correspondents and public speakers; notices regarding minutes; and remote participation details.
Accessible formats and communication supports are available, upon request.
Except where otherwise indicated, reports requiring Council consideration will be presented to Council on Wednesday, July 15, 2026 in Planning and Housing Committee Report 68.
The deadline to register by phone to speak, or submit written comments or visual presentations is 4 pm on Tuesday, July 7, 2026, and the deadline to register by email to speak is 8:30 am on Wednesday, July 8, 2026.
agenda_items.minutes:
These “Summary Minutes” indicate the disposition of items and actions taken at the meeting. This document does not include all of the text that will be included in the full Minutes, such as the record of written and oral submissions. Recorded votes and dissents contained in the Summary Minutes are draft until the full Minutes of the meeting are confirmed by the Committee. The draft of the full Minutes (for confirmation) will be published with the agenda for the next regular Committee meeting and, once confirmed, will replace this document.The Chair read the following statement at the outset of the meeting pursuant to the Planning Act:
This is a public meeting to consider the proposed Comprehensive Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments listed as Item(s) 5.1 - 5.5 and 5.7 on today’s Agenda.
For the item just mentioned, only those who make oral submissions today or written submissions before the amendments are adopted may appeal the matter to the Ontario Land Tribunal. In addition, the applicant may appeal the matter to the Ontario Land Tribunal if Council does not adopt an amendment within 90 days of receipt of the application for a Zoning By-law Amendment and 120 days for an Official Plan Amendment.
To submit written comments on these amendments, prior to their consideration by City Council on July 15, 2026, please email or call the Committee or Council Coordinator.

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Direction to staff (Councillor A. Troster, on behalf of Councillor S. Menard)
As part of the next steps in the Council-directed review of the Rental Renovation License By-law and additional demolition control protections for tenants, Planning and Housing staff explore our legal authority and implementation path to better protect residents in affordable rental units that could be demolished. This could include re-housing, significant financial incentives for compensation, rent top ups, right of first refusal to return at the same or similar rent, and strict enforcement of negotiated settlements.
Direction to staff (Councillor L. Johnson)
As part of the review of the Renovation License Bylaw, that staff provide data relating to permitting time related to renovation, including permit issuance, but also other factors that could cause delay, including incomplete and non-compliant permit applications. 
Direction to staff (Councillor T. Tierney)
For renovations to buildings defined as “small,” “large” and “complex,” under the Ontario Building Code, provide the average review timelines, both to the issuance of first deficiency letter, and to issuance of the building permit itself.

motions.motion_text:
Report Recommendation(s)
That Planning and Housing Committee recommend Council approve the proposed Rental Renovation Licence By-law as described in this report and in the general form set out in Document 1.

WHEREAS the draft bylaw proposed is an important step towards protecting tenants in Ottawa and joining other municipalities across Ontario; and if approved, the City of Ottawa has the opportunity to create strong legislation that supports tenants: and
WHEREAS sections within Bills 60 and 97 providing additional protection for tenants (i.e., qualified person's report, landlord compliance with personal use claim) have not been enacted and have no timeline for implementation: and
WHEREAS if approved, the draft bylaw will be implemented January 1, 2027; and
WHEREAS in its direction dated June 10, 2026, Council directed staff to include a review of the Rental Renovation Licence By-law on the proposed workplan for the next term of Council; and
WHEREAS if the Rental Renovation License By-law is included in the by-law review workplan approved for the next term of Council, the results of the review of the Rental Renovation Licence By-law are to be brought back to Committee in Q4, 2027; and
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Policy Development department include a review of the rental renovation license bylaw on the proposed by-law review workplan for the next term of Council and, if approved as part of that workplan, that staff bring the results of that review forward in Q4 2027; and
THEREFORE BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the addition of the following elements to the rental renovation by-law be considered as part of that review:

sub_agendas_items.title: Renaming of Mosquito Drive to McEvoy Drive
sub_agendas_items.minutes: Submitted by Councillor G. Gower (on behalf of Councillor S. Desroches)

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS Mosquito Drive is the name of a street in Ward 22 within the Riverside South Business Park; and
WHEREAS McEvoy was approved as a street name through the Commemorative Naming Policy in April 2025 and is available to be used in Ward 22; and
WHEREAS the McEvoy family immigrated from Ireland in 1827 and was instrumental in the development of Ottawa’s rural south; and
WHEREAS the McEvoy & Shields Funeral Home was founded in 1925 by brothers Ambrose and Dominic McEvoy; and
WHEREAS Margaret McEvoy began fostering children in the mid-1930’s for the Children’s Aid Society, cared for over 200 foster children over her lifetime and was awarded the Centennial Medal by the Government of Canada for her tireless service to children; and
WHEREAS Phil McEvoy served as a Councillor in the former Township of Osgoode in the 1970’s; and
WHEREAS it is important that the City of Ottawa continue to recognize and celebrate its local heritage by naming municipal facilities, parks, streets, and public spaces after individuals or families who have made significant contributions to their communities; and
WHEREAS Mosquito Drive currently has no addressed properties on it making now the ideal time to rename the street.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Mosquito Drive in Ward 22 be renamed McEvoy Drive.

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by Councillor T. Tierney:
How many trees has the City lost as a result of the recent storms? Of those, how many trees that came down has the City attempted to save, and what has been the associated cost? Additionally, do we have, and are we reviewing, the species of trees being planted to ensure they are better suited to climate change and increasing wind speeds?
As we have added on more storage tanks for processing of water and waste water, knowing that the water flow restrictors to keep ground water at the surface was a requirement for the tanks and will still be a requirement; When is the last time they have adjusted the flow restrictors based on area of flooding?
